claim: Scx-Cre; Rosa-DTRLSL (ScxLinDTR) mice injected with diphtheria toxin (DT) for 5 consecutive days resulted in 57% depletion of tendon cells in uninjured FDL tendons relative to WT control littermates.
source: This approach resulted in 57% depletion of tendon cells in uninjured ScxLinDTR FDL tendons relative to WT control littermates (p<0.0001) (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing quantification of tendon cell depletion and statistical analysis (p<0.0001), with reference to Figure 1C and D showing the results.

claim: Local DT injections did not induce cell death in the contralateral FDL tendon.
source: Tendon cell number was unaffected in the contralateral FDL, indicating that local DT injections did not induce cell death in locations other than the targeted hind paw (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing no change in tendon cell number in the contralateral control, with reference to Figure 1C and D.

claim: At 24 days post-depletion, there was a 58.9% reduction in total tendon cells in uninjured ScxLinAi9DTR FDL tendons relative to WT control littermates.
source: At 24 days post-depletion, there was a 58.9% reduction in total tendon cells in uninjured ScxLinAi9DTR FDL tendons relative to WT control littermates (p<0.0105) and a 68.48% depletion of ScxLinAi9 cells in ScxLinAi9DTR FDL tendons relative to WT ScxLinAi9 controls (p<0.0068) (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p<0.0105) and reference to Figure 1G and H.

claim: At 24 days post-depletion, there was a 68.48% depletion of ScxLinAi9 cells in ScxLinAi9DTR FDL tendons relative to WT ScxLinAi9 controls.
source: At 24 days post-depletion, there was a 58.9% reduction in total tendon cells in uninjured ScxLinAi9DTR FDL tendons relative to WT control littermates (p<0.0105) and a 68.48% depletion of ScxLinAi9 cells in ScxLinAi9DTR FDL tendons relative to WT ScxLinAi9 controls (p<0.0068) (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p<0.0068) and reference to Figure 1G and H.

claim: At 38 days post-depletion, total tendon cells were reduced by 60.42% in ScxLinAi9DTR tendons relative to WT controls.
source: At 38 days post-depletion, total tendon cells were reduced by 60.42% (p<0.0091), and ScxLinAi9 cells were reduced by 73.65% relative to ScxLinAi9 WT controls (p<0.0045) (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p<0.0091) and reference to Figure 1G and H.

claim: At 38 days post-depletion, ScxLinAi9 cells were reduced by 73.65% relative to ScxLinAi9 WT controls.
source: At 38 days post-depletion, total tendon cells were reduced by 60.42% (p<0.0091), and ScxLinAi9 cells were reduced by 73.65% relative to ScxLinAi9 WT controls (p<0.0045) (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p<0.0045) and reference to Figure 1G and H.

claim: No significant differences in total tendon cell depletion efficiency were found between D24 and D38 post-depletion timepoints.
source: No significant differences in total tendon cell depletion efficiency (p<0.9935) and ScxLinAi9 cell depletion efficiency (p<0.9359) were found between D24 and D38 post-depletion timepoints.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis showing no significant difference (p<0.9935).

claim: No significant differences in ScxLinAi9 cell depletion efficiency were found between D24 and D38 post-depletion timepoints.
source: No significant differences in total tendon cell depletion efficiency (p<0.9935) and ScxLinAi9 cell depletion efficiency (p<0.9359) were found between D24 and D38 post-depletion timepoints.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis showing no significant difference (p<0.9359).

claim: The number of Scx+ cells was significantly reduced in the ScxLinDTR tendons relative to WT littermates.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p=0.0448) and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A &B.

claim: When Scx+ cells were normalized to total cell count, there was a trending reduction of Scx+ cells in ScxLinDTR tendons compared to WT.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p=0.1000) and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ScxLinDTR tendons had a trending decrease in S100a4+ cells relative to WT littermates.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p=0.0941) and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1D &E.

claim: When S100a4+ cells were normalized to total cell count, there was no significant or trending difference between ScxLinDTR and WT groups.
source: Interestingly, when S100a4+ cells were normalized to total cell count, there was no significant or trending difference between groups (p=0.3525), suggesting some remaining tendon cells may begin expressing S100a4 following ScxLincell depletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p=0.3525) and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: ScxLinDTR tendons exhibited a small number of apoptotic cells peripheral to, but not within, the tendon.
source: ScxLinDTR tendons exhibited a small number of apoptotic cells peripheral to, but not within, the tendon suggesting that a 10-day DT washout period was sufficient for all tendon-specific DT-induced cell death to occur (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).

claim: Both ScxLinDTR and WT littermates exhibited PCNA+ cells within the muscle, but not within the tendon.

claim: ScxLinDTR exhibited a few PCNA+ cells within the tendon that were not present in WT.

claim: ScxLinDTR tendons exhibited more F4/80+ macrophages peripheral to the tendon.

claim: Macrophages may be recruited to the tendon to clean up apoptotic tendon cell debris following ScxLin cell depletion.

claim: A trending improvement in MTP Range of Motion (ROM) in ScxLinDTR repairs was observed at day 14, relative to WT littermates.
source: A trending improvement in MTP Range of Motion (ROM) in ScxLinDTR repairs was observed at day 14, relative to WT littermates (WT vs ScxLinDTR, p=0.0711), but this trend was absent by day 28 post-repair (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p=0.0711) and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The trending improvement in MTP ROM in ScxLinDTR repairs at day 14 was absent by day 28 post-repair.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing no significant difference at day 28, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: ScxLinDTR healing tendons did not significantly differ in gliding resistance at either day 14 or 28 post-repair.
source: ScxLinDTR healing tendons did not significantly differ in gliding resistance at either day 14 or 28 post-repair (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing no significant difference in gliding resistance, with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Biomechanical properties were not altered between ScxLinDTR and WT groups at day 14 post-repair.
source: While biomechanical properties were not altered between groups at day 14, both stiffness and maximum load at failure were significantly increased in ScxLinDTR healing tendons relative to wildtype littermates at day 28 post-repair (Stiffness: WT: 6.48 ± 0.75, ScxLinDTR: 11.22 ± 1.83, p=0.0237; Maximum load at failure: WT: 1.54 ± 0.17, ScxLinDTR: 2.44 ± 0.24, p=0.0061) (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing no significant difference at day 14, with reference to Figure 2D and E.

claim: Both stiffness and maximum load at failure were significantly increased in ScxLinDTR healing tendons relative to wildtype littermates at day 28 post-repair.
source: While biomechanical properties were not altered between groups at day 14, both stiffness and maximum load at failure were significantly increased in ScxLinDTR healing tendons relative to wildtype littermates at day 28 post-repair (Stiffness: WT: 6.48 ± 0.75, ScxLinDTR: 11.22 ± 1.83, p=0.0237; Maximum load at failure: WT: 1.54 ± 0.17, ScxLinDTR: 2.44 ± 0.24, p=0.0061) (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis (p=0.0237 for stiffness, p=0.0061 for maximum load) and reference to Figure 2D and E.

claim: Between days 14 and 28, WT tendon stiffness increased by 39.06% while ScxLinDTR stiffness increased by 109.33%.
source: Between days 14 and 28, WT tendon stiffness increased by 39.06% while ScxLinDTR stiffness increased by 109.33%, and WT tendon maximum load at failure increased by 52.48% while ScxLinDTR maximum load at failure increased by 162.37%, indicating that ScxLinDTR repairs heal at an accelerated rate relative to wild-type littermates.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing changes in stiffness between timepoints.

claim: Between days 14 and 28, WT tendon maximum load at failure increased by 52.48% while ScxLinDTR maximum load at failure increased by 162.37%.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing changes in maximum load at failure between timepoints.

claim: ScxLinDTR repairs heal at an accelerated rate relative to wild-type littermates.

evidence: The claim is inferred from the greater percentage increases in stiffness and maximum load at failure in ScxLinDTR compared to WT between days 14 and 28.

claim: There were no apparent differences in tissue morphology between ScxLinDTR and WT groups at days 14 or 28 post-repair.
source: While there were no apparent differences in tissue morphology between groups at days 14 or 28 post-repair (Figure 3B), we wanted to determine if tendon cell depletion prevented formation of the collagen bridge.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual assessment of tissue morphology with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Masson's trichrome staining revealed presence of bridging collagen through the scar in both ScxLinDTR and WT groups at days 14 and 28.
source: Masson's trichrome staining revealed presence of bridging collagen through the scar in both groups at days 14 and 28, indicating that depletion of ScxLin tendon cells does not prevent formation of the bridging collagen matrix (Figure 3C).

claim: Depletion of ScxLin tendon cells does not prevent formation of the bridging collagen matrix.

claim: Depletion of ScxLinAi9 cells prior to injury does not alter the overall ScxLinAi9 content at D14, possibly due to additional labeling of cells that express Scx following injury.
